Auto-generated Summary:

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call — we got Cascade and Redwood. Uh, just to set expectations, this is a scoping call for the POC kickoff and security checklist.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Thanks Jordan. We're excited — we've got pressure from regulatory to make sure PHI never leaks in any logs, and we want to validate latency for our triage models.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Great. High level we'll cover two strands: security/compliance artifacts and the benchmark plan — throughput and latency plus acceptance criteria. Does that align?
[00:42] Dr. Marcus Hale: Yes, also timing. If we can prove performance and security in 3–4 weeks we can go to procurement.
[00:53] Sanjay Patel: Quick note, our security review needs SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001, plus SSO integration with our IdP (we use Okta). Also, RBAC mapping to our internal roles and audit log retention for 3 years.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: Totally understood. We can provide SOC 2 Type II reports and the ISO attestation. For SSO we support SAML 2.0 — most customers use Okta. On RBAC we can map roles to your AD groups, and we have audit logs with configurable retention — default 90 days but we can extend for Enterprise/Private deployments.
[01:36] Iris Chen: When you say extend for Private deployments, do you mean VPC/private control plane? We're evaluating both Hosted and Dedicated.
[01:45] Priya Nair: Yes, for Hosted API we provide tenant-isolation and encrypted-at-rest keys managed by Redwood KMS. For Dedicated or Private (VPC) we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM and longer audit retention. There's a trade-off: Private gives more control but adds ops time.
[02:03] Lena Ortiz: Our main must-haves: (1) no persistent KV caching of PHI by default, (2) keys under our control for patient data encryption, and (3) auditable access logs.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: We can disable prefix caching for specific routes, and for the pilot we can deploy a dedicated pool with customer-managed keys in a BYOK flow. We'll include the steps in the artifact pack.
[02:31] Sanjay Patel: For BYOK we need key rotation policy and support for HSM-backed keys. Also, log integrity is important — can you sign logs or export to our SIEM?
[02:45] Priya Nair: We support secure log forwarding to your SIEM via SFTP/HTTPS or direct cloud logging integrations. For log integrity, we do tamper-evident append-only logs for Dedicated/Private, and can export signatures for audit. I'll follow up with specifics.
[03:00] Dr. Marcus Hale: On performance: our triage model is roughly 512 tokens average with a 1.5k token tail. We expect 200 qps during peak and bursts to 500 qps for short times. Our SLO is P95 latency under 250ms for 512 tokens.
[03:18] Priya Nair: Good — that gives us targets. For P95 <250ms at 200 qps we usually recommend a dedicated pool with optimized quantization and batching policies. For the pilot we can run a benchmark with our recommended instance types and a synthetic load that mirrors your distribution.
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: We also care about quality — small hallucination rates on triage classification. We'll bring a test set for evaluation.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Pilot acceptance criteria suggestion from our side: (A) Security: SOC2 evidence delivered and SSO/SAML configured, KMS tested; (B) Performance: synthetic benchmark meets P95 < 250ms at 200 qps for 512 tokens and no fatal errors at 500 qps burst; (C) Integration: SDK integration with one sample pipeline and end-to-end inference within your environment; (D) Quality: model output within agreed thresholds against your eval set.
[04:11] Marcus Hale: That looks reasonable. Timeline — can we have artifacts by Monday? We need to assess by next Friday to hit exec sign-off the week after.
[04:21] Jordan Lee: We'll aim to send the compliance pack and benchmark plan by Monday 2026-05-18.
[04:29] Sanjay Patel: A couple more security clarifications: key rotation cadence, MFA for admin console, IP allowlisting, and support for SLA-backed audit retention.
[04:41] Aisha Gómez: For MFA we have SSO enforced for all accounts and admins can have 2FA. IP allowlisting is supported on Dedicated and Private. Audit retention SLAs are part of Enterprise contracts — we can surface options in the pricing doc.
[04:56] Iris Chen: Is there a minimal data residency guarantee? We prefer EU data centers for EU patients.
[05:03] Priya Nair: Yes — region pinning is possible for hosted model variants; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in the desired region or Private deployment. We'll mark that down as a constraint.
[05:16] Lena Ortiz: For the benchmark plan, we want the script and synthetic data shape so our infra team can replicate. Also we want separate runs for token length 512 and 1.5k.
[05:28] Priya Nair: We'll provide a load script (k6/JMeter example), configuration for sequence lengths, and the expected metric outputs (RPS, P50/P95/P99, GPU utilization, error rates).
[05:40] Marcus Hale: On the model side: are you recommending a specific variant? We care about a balance of latency and accuracy.
[05:48] Priya Nair: We'll propose two model variants: a performant quantized 8-bit variant for lower latency, and a higher-precision 16-bit variant for quality runs. For the POC we'll test both and compare metrics.
[06:02] Sanjay Patel: Can Redwood guarantee no logs contain raw input data? We need assurance that logs are scrubbed unless explicitly enabled.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: By default we mask or do not persist raw user inputs in logs for Healthcare customers. For debugging cases we can enable full logs but only with your explicit opt-in and key controls.
[06:24] Lena Ortiz: Great. About the pilot environment: do you spin up an isolated test tenant or do we use a staging space?
[06:31] Priya Nair: For pilot we typically create a dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated if you want isolation; otherwise we can use a staging scope on Hosted with strict RBAC and network controls. For compliance reasons you probably want Dedicated with VPC peering.
[06:49] Marcus Hale: Cost question — Dedicated commit vs hosted per-token. We need a rough estimate for the pilot so procurement can provision funds.
[06:57] Jordan Lee: We'll include a pilot pricing sheet — Dedicated short-term reserved pool for the 4-week pilot plus optional burst capacity. It will show trade-offs vs Hosted.
[07:08] Iris Chen: What's an example batch size / concurrency that you tune for? Our workloads are latency-sensitive.
[07:15] Priya Nair: We tune batch size and scheduling to keep per-request latency low — smaller batch sizes for latency-sensitive routes, larger for background embeddings. We'll provide recommended configs for your triage endpoints.
[07:29] Sanjay Patel: On RBAC: we need role mappings to AD groups and fine-grained permissions — e.g., who can request keys, who can export logs, who can deploy model versions.
[07:41] Aisha Gómez: We support RBAC with granular permission sets and SCIM provisioning to keep groups in sync. We'll document the default roles and a mapping example.
[07:52] Lena Ortiz: If anything fails during the benchmark, what's the rollback plan? We don't want partial deploys to send traffic to unvalidated versions.
[07:59] Priya Nair: We support automatic rollbacks and can configure canary traffic. For the pilot we'll set up an automatic fallback to a stable variant if latency or error thresholds are breached.
[08:12] Marcus Hale: Ok that addresses reliability. A couple specific acceptance thresholds from our side: P95 < 250ms at 200 qps, error rate <0.1%, and audit logs delivered to our SIEM within 5 minutes for critical events.
[08:27] Jordan Lee: We'll map those into the benchmark doc and test plan.
[08:33] Iris Chen: Anything else on compliance? Data deletion policies?
[08:38] Sanjay Patel: Yes, we need data deletion on request and a clear deletion lifecycle for cached KV entries and logs. Also proof of deletion for regulatory audit.
[08:49] Priya Nair: We have data deletion APIs and can provide attestations for deletion events in Enterprise/Private. For the pilot we'll show a sample deletion flow and test it end-to-end.
[09:01] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Next, timeline review — if artifacts land Monday, when can we start the test runs?
[09:08] Priya Nair: If we get sample workloads and approve the config by Wednesday, we can start baseline benchmarks Thursday and run the main load tests Friday — that's tight but feasible. Otherwise the following week.
[09:20] Marcus Hale: We prefer start 2026-05-25 for the 4-week pilot. That gives our infra time to whitelist IPs and set up SIEM endpoints.
[09:29] Jordan Lee: I'll propose a kickoff calendar invite for 2026-05-25 and include the runbook.
[09:36] Aisha Gómez: On governance: we'll add a quarterly review checkpoint in the pilot so we capture security/regression learnings.
[09:44] Sanjay Patel: For the SIEM integration, we need log schemas and sample events so we can map them to our detection rules.
[09:53] Priya Nair: We'll attach an event schema and sample logs in the artifact pack.
[10:00] Iris Chen: Any limitations in function/tool-calling or structured outputs we should know about for our downstream parsers?
[10:08] Priya Nair: We support structured outputs and function-like calls, but we'll validate serialization and ensure the SDK returns stable schemas for your parsers.
[10:18] Lena Ortiz: One last note: procurement will want to see liability clauses for PHI handling — do you have a template?
[10:25] Jordan Lee: Yes, procurement language and clause templates are part of the legal pack. I'll include a starter SOW and data processing addendum.
[10:33] Marcus Hale: Ok good. Let's do a quick recap of owners.
[10:36] Jordan Lee: Recap — Jordan: compliance artifacts + legal pack by Mon 5/18; Priya: benchmark plan + load scripts by Tue 5/19; Sanjay: internal security checklist + SIEM endpoints by Wed 5/20; Lena: sample workloads by Sun 5/17. Schedule pilot kickoff for 5/25 pending infra prep.
[10:56] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone. We'll review artifacts and confirm kickoff.
[11:02] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links (SOC2, ISO, benchmark sheet, runbook).

End of transcript.
